Too many tasks and too much noise? Ilseon shows only one thing to focus on. Ilseon is an ADHD task manager and minimalist daily planner designed to solve executive dysfunction. Built for neurodivergent focus, it helps reduce noise and overwhelm. Stop the context-switching and manage your day with a neurodivergent-friendly tool that helps you do what matters right now.

Focus and Flow: The Ilseon Method

Ilseon helps you cut through context-switching fatigue and achieve a calmer rhythm. Capture tasks the moment they appear, assign each one a Context (like Work, Family, or Projects), and let the Daily Dashboard show only what deserves your attention right now.

Sub-tasks for Project Clarity

To combat analysis-paralysis on large projects, you can now break down any task into sequential sub-tasks. When the parent task is active, the dashboard shows only the steps required, enforcing single-step focus until the entire goal is achieved.

Zero-Friction Capture & Voice Inbox

Great ideas and complex to-do lists don't always happen when you're ready to type. For divergent thinkers and users who prefer a spoken workflow, Ilseon integrates a powerful capture system: • Quick Capture: Log tasks in seconds, keeping them out of your head and safely stored. • Idea Inbox: Designed specifically to capture non-task mental clutter—fleeting ideas, random thoughts, or things to look up later—so they don't derail your current focus. • Notes View: Convert any fleeting idea into a long-term, structured note using simple Markdown. This eliminates the need for separate note-taking apps and centralises all your knowledge within Ilseon. • Voice Inbox: Moves beyond basic speech-to-text. It creates a dedicated space for raw audio capture. Record notes or complex instructions with a single tap. The audio file are saved as a "Voice Memo" locally. • Privacy First: All recordings, ideas and tasks are saved locally on your device.

Contexts keep your responsibilities neatly separated so they don’t compete for attention. When it’s time to focus, the Dashboard acts as your “front line,” filtering out everything except your immediate priority.

show_hn.title: Show HN: Ilseon, as a GTD "Capture" App

quotes.text:
I’ve always struggled with the Capture phase. Most apps feel too heavy in the moment. Even coming up with a title can be enough to break the flow.

My app Ilseon (Android) addresses that specific problem. It’s not a full GTD system or project manager. It’s a targeted task manager designed to reduce mental noise and help users focus on one thing at a time.

Ilseon has GTD elements in its workflow though:

* Fast capture
Tasks and ideas can be captured with almost no structure. No required titles, tags, or projects at the moment of capture.

* Voice capture for hands-busy moments
When typing isn’t practical (walking, driving), I record a short voice memo. Optionally, if you add a Gemini API key, Ilseon can extract tasks from the transcript, but this is strictly optional and happens after capture, not during.

* An idea inbox
There’s a separate scratchpad for thoughts that aren’t quite tasks yet. During a review, these can be promoted into tasks or notes, or discarded.

* Reflection after completion
Completion isn’t the end. A small reflection step encourages reviewing what was actually done.

* Local-first storage
Audio is saved as standard .m4a files in a local folder (Recordings/ilseon/).

I’m looking for feedback from people who care about a clean capture process. Do you experience friction during capture with your current tools, especially when you’re away from your desk?

GitHub: https://github.com/cladam/ilseon
